entities.name: Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Al-Arqam ibn Abī al-Arqam (unknown – 673 CE) was a pivotal companion of Prophet Muhammad, playing a crucial role in the early Muslim community.








 Al-Arqam ibn Abī al-Arqam was the owner of the house where the early Muslim community held its meetings, facilitating the community's growth and development.








 This house became a sanctuary for the community, hosting key events and gatherings that shaped the Islamic faith.








 Al-Arqam's association with the early Muslim community not only cemented his place in Islamic history but also underscores the significance of community in the early days of Islam.








 The role of community in shaping Islamic identity and practice remains a vital aspect of the faith to this day.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Arqam ibn Abī al-Arqam played a crucial role in the early Muslim community, contributing to the development and refinement of Islamic teachings and practices in Medina. His association with the Prophet Muhammad and the early Muslim community underscores the significance of community in the early days of Islam.
